newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals mostly up, palladium buoyant.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals mostly up, palladium buoyant.

text.p: Tokyo precious metals futures ended mostly firmer on Thursday with help from stronger bullion prices, and of these, palladium futures were particularly buoyant, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from flat to seven yen per gram higher, with the most-active benchmark October contract ending three yen per gram higher at 1,361 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from two yen to nine yen per gram firmer, with benchmark October finishing up six at 430.
"Backed by sharp gains in spot palladium, trade houses bought palladium futures from the opening," one trader said.
But price gains in palladium futures were capped by active profit-taking by private investors.

Traders said expected declines in global palladium supplies in calendar 1996, as noted in a report by British platinum group metal refiner Johnson Matthey Plc, was attributable to firmer spot palladium prices. But Japanese traders said there was little room for spot palladium prices to rise further.
In the gold futures market, private investors who were generally buyers earlier in the day, switched to selling later to take profits, the traders said.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $383.20/383.50 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $383.05/383.45 in New York on Wednesday.
The precious metals market was awaiting for remarks from senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara later today to see if his comments provide a key to the currency market.

In platinum futures, private investors were tending to take profits, while Japanese traders sold spot platinum in arbitrage trade. Benchmark October platinum was two yen per gram higher at 1,381 yen. Benchmark October silver was 0.5 yen per 10 grams stronger at 179.0 yen. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7391
